summary: A static field is shared by every object of the class, and a static method is called on the class itself. Fields without static belong to one object.
notes: static int count = 0; exists once, no matter how many Student objects you make.
A static method like isValidId() cannot use this or instance fields like name.
leo.school = ... changes the one shared static field. Write Student.school so this is clear.
pitfall: Using an instance field inside a static method, like name in isValidId(), causes the compile error "non-static variable name cannot be referenced from a static context".
